utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before I'll invite the Prosecution to call its next witness, I'd like to deal with a few procedural matters. I'd first like to address the Prosecution with instructions from this Chamber. The Prosecution will recall that at the pre-trial conference on the 1st of March of 2007, the Chamber said the following, and I quote: "On the basis of the information you have provided until now, the Chamber grants the Prosecution 125 hours examination-in-chief to present its case. This is not to encourage the use of 125 hours if less would do, and this is not a decision for eternity. As I said before today, the Chamber will take a flexible approach and will also look at how the time is used and reserve all rights to adapt the number of hours granted if good cause exists to do so." That's the end of the quote. This was at the pages 350 to 351, and you may also wish to refer to the discussion on the pages 684 and 685, where a typographical error or perhaps my own error of pronunciation is discussed relating to the above text. Following the pre-trial conference, the Chamber has issued the Prosecution with several warnings that examination-in-chief is taking much longer than estimated. We have advised you on the Prosecution's side to be more focused in your questioning of witnesses, yet you have continued to run over your estimates. This is despite the fact that Rule 92 ter, which is meant to save court time, is being increasingly relied on by you to introduce evidence in paper form. The results of this consumption of time are to be seen in the two tables that have been handed around, if they have been handed around. Not yet. Then they should be handed around. Are they available? Well, then I'll tell you what you find on it and you'll receive it soon, because the results of this consumption are to be seen in the two tables. I refer you first of all to the table entitled: "Main Database Report Number 3." As of the end of the testimony of Witness 6, you have used up almost 15 hours more than you had estimated before the witness in question. You would then turn to the table entitled: "Main database Report Number 2," which will be handed out to you, which shows that you have completed 28 witnesses, not counting the Chamber witness Maklen Misha and not counting, of course, Shefqet Kabashi. You've now used up 50.3 per cent of your allocated time. This means that you have just under 62 and a half hours to present the remainder of your case. The Chamber would like to receive from the Prosecution an updated witness list. At the moment we are -- at the moment we are working off the 2nd of March, 2007, list. Some witnesses have been taken off that list, whereas the status of others has changed, especially within the framework of the Rules 92 bis, 92 ter, and 92 quater. If you would consider, for example, the witness with pseudonym 14. He is classified as a 92 ter witness in annex A of your motion of the 19th of February, 2007. To be precise, he is listed as a 92 bis witness who should appear for cross-examination, but this is practically equivalent to him being a 92 ter witness. Now, on the 24th of May, 2007, the Chamber denied your application to subpoena Witness 14. What then is his current status? Do you still plan to keep him on your witness list? Moreover, the updated witness list should ensure that the time allocations for the remaining witnesses add up to the hours remaining in the Prosecution's case, which, as at the end of Witness 6, stood at just under 62 and a half hours. The Prosecution is given until Tuesday, the 19th of June, to file its updated witness list, and this concludes the Chamber's remark on the matters. I was informed that the main database reports number 3 and number 2 will be delivered within the next couple of minutes. The next item, the Chamber announces that the Defence submissions on Witness 30 have not persuaded the Chamber that it should not issue the subpoena requested by the Prosecution. I move to my next item, and that is that I'd like to ask the Defence if there are any objections to the protective measures for -- the protective measures requested in the 12th written motion for protective measures, which initially was numbered the 11th motion, but now has been corrected as the 12th motion, that is in relation to the witness -- not the witness who will start his testimony today because no protective measures are sought in relation for that witness, but the witness then to follow after the witness will start to testify today. Is -- if you can't give an answer now, the Chamber would like to hear from you whether perhaps later this afternoon you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, most certainly I would have thought immediately after the first break we would certainly so far as we are concerned be able to give Your Honour a definitive response. There are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- there are one or two matters relating to both of the first witnesses that at a convenient moment before we proceed I need to raise with Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll give you an opportunity, but I still have a few other items on my list. After the first break, Mr. Guy-Smith, Mr. Harvey, would that be possible for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be absolutely fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And for us, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I move to a couple of matters that are in some way related. The Chamber has not received reports in respect to some of the subpoenas the Chamber has issued. That is, first of all, in relation to subpoenaed Witness 52, then -- so the Chamber would like to -- if any of the parties, and of course especially the Prosecution who calls these witnesses, is aware of any developments in view of the subpoenas being served or whatever other developments in that context, the Chamber would like to be informed. The same would be true for the witness which has been subpoenaed to appear on Thursday, the 14th of June; and the same question also arises in view of a subpoena for a witness to appear on Wednesday, the 20th of June; and in relation to a witness which is subpoenaed to appear on Thursday, the 21st of June. Of course, the Chamber would like to know whether the subpoenas are served upon these witnesses, but also the Chamber wonders that if there would be any obstacle for the witnesses to appear, whether the Prosecution has developed any alternative scenario, but of course then we would have to know something about it. The Chamber wants to avoid that we are sitting in court and then hear the report that the witness doesn't appear and that we have no alternative scenario to proceed upon. So therefore, the Chamber is urging the Prosecution to closely monitor what happens with the subpoenas, to inform the Chamber about any development in that context the OTP has knowledge of, and then also to be informed on whatever the consequences. Of course, if the witnesses will appear as scheduled, there's no problem, but if there's any obstacle there to present alternative scheduling. I don't know, Mr. Di Fazio, whether you could give us information now at this moment on the four witnesses I mentioned, but -- and I don't know whether it can be done in open session, but I leave it to you at this moment. If you would prefer to respond to that after the break, then of course you may do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think in the interests of accuracy that that's a better idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'll move to my -- no, I have no further matters on my list. Then, Mr. Emmerson, you asked to address the Chamber on certain matters. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There are disclosure issues arising in respect of both of the next two witnesses. I pause before I use the name of the first witness. My understanding is that no protective measures have been sought in respect of that witness and that there is no difficulty in me using his name in open court, and I see Mr. Di Fazio shaking his head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The first witness who is due to testify today is Miomir Stosic. Yesterday evening electronically the Prosecution disclosed a batch of material relevant to the named victim in the count to which the evidence of this witness is relevant. The material was disclosed almost exclusively in B/C/S and it has not been possible for the Defence to read or understand let alone assimilate it. We understand that searches are currently being made within the Prosecution's files to determine whether English translations of those documents can be made available; but given the timetable, it is unlikely that they can be produced and assimilated in sufficient time for cross-examination on those documents, if there is cross-examination on those documents, to take place immediately after evidence in chief. For my part, I've given some consideration as to whether it would be the most fruitful use of time for me to suggest that I should cross-examine as far as I can before the documents are assimilated. The reality is that such cross-examination as I anticipate having for this witness, as matters currently stand, is unlikely to occupy sufficient time to enable the Trial Chamber's time this afternoon to be used as productively as it ought to be, which brings me to the next witness, in respect of whom there is an application for protective measures and whose name --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I interrupt you for one second. Could Mr. Di Fazio inform us -- not in detail, but give us any impression of what these disclosed documents are about. Is that something that sheds a new light on matters or whether it just confirms or --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: They're mainly, as I understood it, disclosure relating to the victim, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The relative of this coming witness, so they were principally, if I recall, of scientific nature. There certainly aren't any statements or anything from that deceased person or anything like that. I didn't think there would be anything in there that would particularly excite the Defence's interest, but that's from my perspective of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has it been explored whether what we find in those documents would concern matters on which the parties do agree? I don't know to what extent I earlier understood, for example, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: There may be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that DNA identification is accepted. I don't know whether that's true for this -- for the victim -- the relative of this witness. If that would be true, then it -- if these are all kind of doctor's report -- I don't know what it is, but if it would be that, one could wonder what's the use of -- of presenting them if they deal with a matter that is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I might add, that's what I suspect most of the documents are, because I only became aware, unfortunately, of this controversy when I came into court. And I haven't had a chance to look at the documents for which there are no translations. And so I -- when I say to you I think they are mainly scientific documents, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Di Fazio --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I suspect that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- do I understand you well that the material that was disclosed to Mr. Emmerson yesterday evening late that you say, I saw that material only just before I entered court? I would have expected you --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if it was disclosed to the Defence yesterday, that you would have used this morning to -- at least to understand, even if not in detail, but at least to get yourself acquainted with what these documents approximately tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It was mainly material that related, as I said, to the deceased. I had gone through a lot of the material, some of the B/C/S material, and made arrangements for it to be disclosed on the basis of a look at the material and a decision as to whether or not it fell within the Rules and should be made available to the Defence. I didn't go through the documents chapter in verse because they didn't interest the Prosecution considerably. So that's the assessment that I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might be that the matter will be resolved. It might be that there still is a problem. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I obviously don't know how Mr. Di Fazio is in the position to be familiar in detail with the contents of these reports. It may be that he scanned them with a B/C/S reader. The -- I'm to some extent in Your Honour's hands, but in practical terms, knowing that the Prosecution has disclosed material relating to the alleged victim of this count and knowing that on the evidence there is some considerable uncertainty about the circumstances surrounding the disappearance and fatality involved and without going into detail knowing that whilst DNA is not in issue as far as the Defence of Mr. Haradinaj is concerned, there are forensic issues relevant to this witness and this victim which I would want it, albeit briefly, to explore with this witness and perhaps in much more detail with witnesses to come. I would be reluctant to accept a first-blush view of Mr. Di Fazio's -- on documents he can't read in a language he understands about whether or not it may have material of potential assistance to the Defence. What I'm really seeking to do is to make a proposal which makes the most efficient use of the Trial Chamber's time this afternoon, and I raised with Mr. Di Fazio just before Your Honours sat whether there was -- an alternative course of action which would involve him calling this witness to give his evidence in chief and then moving immediately on to the evidence in chief of the witness to follow. But may I say that there is a comparable problem, although perhaps not so acute, in respect of the witness to follow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that you're now moving to your next disclosure issue or --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- I'm really putting them all before Your Honours so you're really in a position to see which direction you would like to give for the conduct of these proceedings this afternoon. Just before you sat we were provided with a lever-arch file containing 23 -- I'm sorry, 18 documents relevant to the count in respect of which the second witness is due to give evidence. Now, as -- I have somebody to my left looking through the material as I speak because obviously I have not had an opportunity to acquaint myself with the contents of the file which was not disclosed electronically in advance. But as I understand it - and I'll be corrected if I'm wrong - the documents we have been provided are in the majority in English and therefore it will be possible to assimilate them, but again not possible to assimilate them whilst evidence in chief is taking place. So my practical suggestion, if it works, would be for both witnesses to give their evidence in chief today and for us then to adjourn and assimilate the disclosure which has been provided in the not-entirely-helpful order in which it has been provided overnight and then for cross-examination to commence tomorrow if that is a course that is favourable to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, the suggestion made by Mr. Emmerson, would you like to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. While, I leave the matter in the Trial Chamber's hands. I can say this, that the proposed course of action would not greatly inconvenience the Prosecution, and I'm ready to proceed with my witness. I understand Mr. Kearney will be ready to proceed with his witness, and he's been notified that it may move up in time if this course of action is adopted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I additionally ask you, what explains this late disclosure of documents -- let's first focus on the first witness to start his testimony today, that's at least how I now call him. Why was that disclosed 15 hours before the start of his testimony and not any earlier. Is that new material or did the witness bring it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, it wasn't new material. I think the problem, unless I'm wrong, is that there's an absence of English translation for a lot of the B/C/S material that was -- that went in the unfortunately late disclosure. And that's probably, I gather, what has caused the Defence problems. The Prosecution is now making -- will locate all available - and I stress the word available - English translations and provide them to the Defence as soon as possible. And I can't guarantee that there are English translations for each and every document that was given to them in B/C/S, but the problem arose in finding matching English translations and sending those to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try and understand. One way or the other you identified the document as relating to the deceased relative of the witness. You suggest that the absence of an English translation causes some trouble to the Defence. I can imagine that it caused you some trouble as well, and I asked myself what made you pay attention to these documents which are not translated into English but which you, for one reason or another, identified as relevant for the -- today's witness. And if you have done that before, why have you not told the Defence that you identified some documents which -- where you've not yet found English translations but you'll do your utmost best, I mean why did this not happen last Friday --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That should have happened -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or Thursday or Wednesday or preferably Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I regret that, if Your Honours please, and I will try and ensure that that doesn't occur in respect of upcoming witnesses. The Prosecution does --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you also then, please, next time not present the matter as something which causes problems to the Defence, but where you don't wait for the Defence to tell us that there's a disclosure problem. But to report that spontaneously to the Chamber that you failed documents which you identified as relevant for the witness, that you failed, first of all, to disclose them in their original language earlier; and that you failed to timely check whether there were any translations available. Let's move on. I think enough has been said about this. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is one other matter, and I wonder if I might simply raise it briefly. It arises out of the indication that Your Honour gave a moment ago in relation to the ruling concerning the subpoena application in respect of Witness 30. Without going into details at this stage, Your Honour will recall that the Defence submission in respect of that subpoena raised two central questions about two other witnesses, one of whom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- is a named victim and a witness to certain matters which Witness 30 would testify about, and one of whom is a named perpetrator allegedly of one of the counts in respect of which Witness 30 was due to give evidence. Your Honours will recall from the correspondence summarized in the Defence submission that in respect of the first of those two individuals the Defence have been requesting now for some time an explanation and disclosure from the Defence -- from the Prosecution of what can only be Rule 68 material which led the Prosecution to choose to abandon at the 11th hour that witness as a witness for the Prosecution. Similarly, so far as the other witness is concerned, Your Honours will recall - and it's referred to in the motion - an occasion in which Mr. Di Fazio assured the Trial Chamber that a suspect interview which had been conducted with that witness very shortly before the hearing would be disclosed to the Defence the following day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me cut this short. When I indicated, Mr. Emmerson, that the submissions on Witness 30 had not persuaded the Chamber that it should not issue the subpoena, this was not meant to mean that the issues raised for which you applied for delay of our decision are not serious anymore. Mr. Di Fazio, you've certainly seen the matters raised and which caused the Defence to ask for a delay in deciding upon your motion. When do you think that you could further address those matters? I'm not going into detail either at this moment. That is one witness not on the list anymore, another witness where Mr. Emmerson said that -- perhaps you check that over the break as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, finally in relation to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I haven't personally handled that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can get that information to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: After the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I just need some time to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it may assist Mr. Di Fazio's recollection, I think he's dealt personally with both of the two witnesses at one time or another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I also in respect of that witness place one matter formally on the public record. I have been concerned to know for some time and have asked of the Prosecution orally why it was that a decision was taken that Witness 30 should not be called as a witness in the Limaj trial, given that his statement includes direct allegations of having witnessed a crime committed by one of the accused in that trial and being in a position to identify that individual. I was concerned to know whether the Prosecution as a whole or the Prosecutors in that case had reached that decision because of a view that they had taken adverse to that witness as to his credibility. And I made the request of Mr. Re orally at the beginning of this year, and I wish, if I may, to place on the record a -- the contents of a three-line response which I've received in writing from Mr. Re on the 1st of February which says this: "In response to your oral query about why the Prosecution did not call," the witness, I won't mention his name, "as a witness in the Limaj, Bala, and Musliu trial, I confirm that his proposed testimony concerned issues outside of the indictment period and was not relevant to that case." It may be that that explanation will require some revisiting in due course, and I think it right and necessary that it be placed on the public record at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's now on the record. Mr. Di Fazio, are you ready to call your next witness, which is, as was said before, Miomir Stosic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I am, and I hope to do so shortly. But perhaps before we do, do -- is the course proposed by Mr. Emmerson going to be adopted by the Trial Chamber; namely, that we proceed with the evidence in chief of both of these witnesses today and reserve their cross-examination until tomorrow to alleviate this disclosure problem?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, the Chamber may well follow the suggestion, but we'll consider it during the break and that means that we could start now with the examination-in-chief of the first witness. Perhaps -- you certainly should prepare for the next witness to be called before Mr. Stosic is cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure that Mr. Kearney is springing into action as we speak. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stosic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth before you give your testimony in this court. The text of the solemn declaration is now handed out to you by Madam Usher, and I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stosic. Please be seated. Mr. Stosic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Di Fazio. Mr. Di Fazio is sitting over there -- or standing over there. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Stosic, I'd like to get some personal details from you, please. Could you tell us if the details that I now recount to you are correct; these are details concerning yourself. You were born on the 26th of July, 1969, in Pec, and you are of Serbian ethnicity. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In 1998 you lived in Belo Polje, which is just on the outskirts of Pec, along with your father; your mother; your brother, Zoran; and his wife. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your father, Velizar, was born in 1935. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know his actual birth date, the full date, or only the year in which he was born?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Just the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want you to tell us, please, some details about your father, your late father. Did he live throughout his life in Pec?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In 1998, was he a retired man?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do you know how long prior to 1998 he had retired?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Four to five years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell the Trial Chamber what his job had been prior to his retirement?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: He was a driver, and then he was a receptionist.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of receptionist precisely?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: He actually worked in the security service of a certain company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And I -- that's what I'd like to be clear about, this security service. What did that actually mean? Where did he -- where was he located during the day when he worked and what were his actual day-to-day duties when he worked in -- at the security service, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: He worked in 24-hour shifts every other day. He guarded the company's administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What company? Where was the company's administration building located?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: The administration building was in Pec, and the name of the company was Srbija Sume and before it was a forestry company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was Srbija Sume somehow a company dealing with forest -- the forest in Kosovo, forest lands in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. What did your father do after he retired, some four to five years before 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: He worked as a farmer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stosic, does your first name happen to be Miomir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where did your father work as a farmer?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: In the village where we lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did your -- did your family own any land outside of the village in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: In Brzenik, 4 kilometres from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And let's get this clear, okay. First of all, where was your family home in 1998, the place that you went to sleep in every night with your mother and father and your brother Zoran and his wife? Where was that house located?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Belo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And Belo Polje, I believe, is only -- either part of Pec or not very far from Pec, is that correct, to the south of Pec?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Part of Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did your father or did your family, I should say, own any other land not located in Belo Polje?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: The question is not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I don't know whether you're asking the same as you did before where you asked: "Did the family own any land outside of the village where you lived." The answer was: "Yes. "Where was that? "In Brzenik, 4 kilometres from the village." Is that what you're seeking?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Not quite, if Your Honours please, but I'll deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is Brzenik very far from a place called Lodza?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: It was together with Lodza, it was part of Lodza.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If your father went to visit his -- his land, where would he normally describe himself as going, to Brzenik or to Lodza?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: In Brzenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like you to look at a photograph, please, on the screen that will appear in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can the witness be shown 65 ter number 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Please look at the photograph of this individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can move on while that -- while it's being dealt with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Registrar has resolved the matter. Yes. It should appear soon on our screens. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you recognise the individual in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who is it?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: That's my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that Velizar Stosic?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I tender the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam -- Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 341 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P341, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P341, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, let's get back to the issue of the plot of land that your father worked. Following his retirement, did he go to this plot of land in Brzenik from time to time?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And how would he normally travel there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Mostly by bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do you know the village of Lodza itself, the actual village? Have you been there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes, once.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How far is -- do you know -- can you tell us how far this land was from that village?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: It was that Lodza actually was kind of -- continued on from there, it kept growing, so that's the place where actually Lodza began.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did the trip take from your house, your family home, in Belo Polje to this place where your family held some land?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: What do you mean how long did it take?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long, once he got on his bicycle, would it take him to ride from your house to the land that was owned by your family? How long? How many minutes?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: 15 to 20 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I want you to turn your mind to 1998. Was your father visiting that plot of land in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And about how often would he go there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the need, perhaps 15, 20 days, maybe 10 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, in July of 1998 did your father go there, to the plot of land?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember the date in July or the dates in July that he went to the plot of land?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: The 17th of July, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What were you doing on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I went to work, and then when I came back my mother said that the father -- my father had gone to tend to the field and that he never came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. In that period of time, July of 1998, what was the security situation like in your area?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: The situation was tense.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did that affect your father's going to visit his plot of land or the plot of land that was held by your family?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Tell the Trial Chamber in what way it affected -- affected his visits.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Personal safety. It wasn't safe to move around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And why not in particular? What was -- what made it unsafe?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Well, that was the general situation, that's what it was like, it was tense.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did that have any effect on your father's visits to the family plot of land?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Perhaps a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that something that you know or something that you speculate? Do you actually know if it affected his visits or not?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you would like me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let's move on. Now, you said your father last went there in -- on the 17th of July, 1998. Did you ever see him again?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know if he took his bicycle on the 17th of July, 1998, when he went to his field?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that something he normally did, get there on his bicycle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question has been put and answered by the witness, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: After the 17th of July, 1998, did you ever see your father's bicycle?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you try and explain to the Trial Chamber the circumstances under which you next saw your father's bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: With a police escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just start at the beginning and tell the Trial Chamber how it happened. Did you go and speak to the police? Did they come and speak to you? Had you gone to the field yourself? How did it actually transpire that you saw again your father's bicycle?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: The police came to my house to get me. They said that that part which was controlled by some army had been liberated and that it was possible to go and to look at the bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know what army the police were talking about?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: No, I don't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: After your father left on the 17th of July, 1998, and he didn't come back, did you go to the fields looking for him, at that field that was held by your family, or did your brother Zoran go there, or did your mother go there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Any reason why not?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: He wasn't there in the field. There was no need to go there anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How did you know that he wasn't there in the field anymore?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Because the police had searched that whole area around the field and the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how long after did -- your father left on the 17th of July, 1998, did the police come and tell you -- did the police come and get you and say to you that it was possible to go and look at the bicycle, about how long after?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Approximately a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in between the 17th of July, 1998, and the police telling you that the bicycle had been found in the field did you or your brother Zoran or your mother go to the field looking for your father?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: There was just me, no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. There was just you, no one else. Did you go to the field?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that day when the police was there, and I didn't go anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Anyway, you did not go to the field after the 17th of July for a period of about a month. That's correct, do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you, indeed, see a bicycle in the field that was owned by your family?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Whose bicycle was it?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: It was ours from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was it actually located in the field itself?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: It was right at the beginning where the field began, maybe a couple of metres into the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, after this, or rather, I should say after the 17th of July, 1998, did you make any attempts to locate your father or find him?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I did not. All I did is report that he was missing to the International Red Cross in Pec as well as to the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you -- did the police ever seek your assistance, more details, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know of a place called Zlopek?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have you ever been there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Under what circumstances and when did go there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Under a police escort, in order to identify a body that they believed was not my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't follow that. What special expertise did you have in identifying bodies that were not that of your father? I don't follow. Why would the police ask you to do that?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: To look at the body to see whether that was my father, because he had been missing for more than a month before that. They believed that it wasn't possible that this victim was my father, so I went there personally to look, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for explaining that. That's clear. Thank you. And when you went there, was it -- were there policemen in attendance?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you help or participate in the recovery of the body?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there any cameras there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who operated the camera?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Technicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know if they were police technicians?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there anyone there in custody?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was a man in civilian clothing with handcuffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to what that person was doing there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: He showed the place where the body was buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that something you know or something someone told you? How do you know that, basically?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I know because he was there and he indicated with his hand where the body was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What ethnicity was that person?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever go to any other such scenes that you just described, apart from Zlopek?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sorry, before I leave Zlopek in particular, can you remember approximately when you went to Zlopek to try and identify your father?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Maybe about a month and a half after he disappeared, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, you started to tell us about other places that you went to. Apart from Zlopek, can you tell us the next place that you went to?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: To Radonjic Lake, the canal of Radonjic Lake and Ljumbarda.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll deal with this this way. Did you go to Ljumbarda and the canal of Radonjic Lake on the same day or on separate days?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: In relation to Zlopek?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about your visit to Radonjic Lake and Ljumbarda. Did you go to those two places on the same day, Ljumbarda and the canal leading into Lake Radonjic on the same day?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember the date that you went there? If you can't remember, just say so, but if you can remember, tell us.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact date, but it was perhaps about two months after my father disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And how did you come to be there? How did you ...

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: The police came and they said that they found bodies, and they sent me to go and see if any of those bodies was the body of my parent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. So the police asked you to attend at that scene, did they?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you remember if you went to Ljumbarda or the canal leading into Lake Radonjic first? Which one did you go to first?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I went to the canal first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you a photograph of the -- an aerial shot of the canal area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: May the witness be shown 65 ter 1220, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that a different aerial photograph from the area than the one as -- that is already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's the same one but unmarked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unmarked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm informed further that it's Exhibit 45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think we're going to need the assistance of the usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm embarking on an exercise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I would really appreciate the usher's assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, now, the usher is going to give you a special magic pencil now, and you can write on the screen with this. I would like you to get the magic pencil and mark on the screen with one small circle the area that you went to when you went to the canal. Now, just look at it carefully. When you've worked out where you went to, could you please indicate that on the screen and a mark will come up.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P342.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Don't touch the screen again, please, Witness. Now, did you ever cross the canal to the other side, or did you stay on that side of the canal on that day that you visited this area?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: No, I did not cross over to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you notice any cement -- or were there any cement walls?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever walk away from that area down towards the lake or in the opposite direction, or did you remain in that area that you've marked?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I did go towards the lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How far?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Maybe a kilometre or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who did you go with?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: With the police and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just the police or other people?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Well, there were other people there, but I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you for that. Thanks for that clarification. When you were at the point or the area close to the area that you've marked on this map, did you see any bodies?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know how many bodies you saw on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Five or six, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were they decomposed?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I appreciate the difficulty, but I'm very anxious that Mr. Di Fazio not lead the witness about any aspect of this part of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you -- when you were at the lake, did you see any cars?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry, at the canal, this area that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The same problem that was just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, with respect, that's not leading a witness. A man standing there would have opened his eyes, and he would have seen many things. He would have seen the sky, birds, and so on, other people, policemen, leaves trees, rocks, et cetera. One must be able to ask a witness a basic innocent question like: Did you see any vehicles at the location? It's not suggestive of the answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- And my submission is not -- I'm not engaging any leading sort of mischief by asking that particular question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is overruled. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see any vehicles at the area that -- that you were at? I'm talking about the area that you've indicated.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where were the vehicle -- where were the vehicles located -- vehicle or vehicles located?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, that misstates --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were several --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- the witness's testimony. He was asked if he saw vehicles, and he now has refined his question and that certainly is a new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now he's suggesting one of two answers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Stosic, when you said -- when you were asked whether you saw vehicles, you answered yes. Did you intend to say that you saw one or did you see more vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Several vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were they police vehicles or army vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: There were police vehicles there, a fire brigade vehicle or vehicles, and civilian vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. All in working order or capable of being driven?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: The ones up there, yes, but there was one vehicle in the canal and it wasn't possible to drive that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours would just bear with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want to show the witness two clips. They're not in e-court, they're in Sanction apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like you to have a look at these video-clips and just absorb -- just look at them, okay, just look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: They can be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I'd now like you to -- well, perhaps I should stop there. Did you -- did you see anything in that video-clip?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I saw a car in a canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd now like the witness to be shown a second clip, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, has this clip or this portion of the clip been exhibited already? And what number would it be so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's a portion of an exhibit. It's one of the forensic exhibits. I can give you the answer to that in just a moment, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a portion of the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, it's a portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: As is the next clip that I intend to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can I proceed to show the next clip to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you would rewind that so we can look at it from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Perhaps that could be done. If we could go to the previous clip and look at it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The exhibit number is being looked up and we'll have that for Your Honours, if Your Honours please. Now, can the witness be shown the second clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have a look at this as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. For the Prosecution's purposes, the clip can be stopped at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you look at that clip and did you see anything in that clip; if so, what?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: I saw a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you saw the -- you said earlier in your evidence, you testified that you saw a car. When you saw the car, can you tell us if it was upside down or -- yes, upside down or is it in the condition you can see it in this particular clip? You can see the red colour of the vehicle. Can you remember? And remember, don't -- if you're not sure, make sure that you tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: It was upside down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you do anything in respect of that car?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Well, I helped in the effort to pull the car out of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And how was that done?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: With ropes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I will seek to tender those two clips into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't know if you want them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If they are already -- if the whole of the video is already in evidence, then is there any need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, for my purposes, no. As long as we -- it is part -- it is part of another exhibit in the case but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have the number for us --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it would certainly help and then we can say exactly for the record what portion was shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm looking for the exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder whether it -- with all respect, whether it might be the simplest of all to give a fresh exhibit number to those two clips, and I say that because Your Honours will have seen the time-line at the bottom of them and it may be a matter of some importance to be absolutely clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then -- we could be clear to the extent whether it's an earlier exhibit, yes or no. The first portion that was played went from 14 minutes, 54.8 seconds, up to approximately 15 minutes, 7 seconds, so the whole portion played was approximately 12 seconds; whereas the second portion started at 1 hour, 25 minutes, 01 seconds dot 8, so almost 25.02, and went up to 1, 25 minutes, 20.2 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Unless I'm much mistaken - and I'll be corrected if I'm wrong because one's familiar with some of these pieces of film but they do look alike - unless I'm much mistaken these are two separate pieces of film from which you've been played excerpts which, on the face of it, were taken four days apart from one another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, you're invited to clarify exactly whether this is in evidence or not and then the Chamber will decide whether, for these two clips, specific exhibit numbers will be assigned. But at least it's on the record now already what minutes have been played.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, and I have an opportunity now to check. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'm coming --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Mr. Di Fazio, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right. I can indicate I'm drawing very close to the end of my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would say it's just a matter of a couple of minutes, then we could continue; otherwise, I would like to have a break now. Are you talking about how many minutes, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Maybe another five or six minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, then, it would be worthwhile to continue for such a period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And Your Honours will convey your decision after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Sorry, I momentarily misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, after you had been to Lake Radonjic, did you ever go to Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Not on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how long after did you go to Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Maybe seven days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson and Mr. Guy-Smith, does the objection against leading also stand in relation to this episode?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what did you do in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Well, all the bodies from the Radonjic Lake were moved to the Pastrik Hotel in Djakovica. I went there because I had been unable to identify my father on that day. I had to wait until everything was exhumed and taken there, and then I went there to identify my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How did you come to go there? Did you go there on your own initiative or did the police mention it to you? How did it transpire?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: The police notified me about the day when I was supposed to go there and look. I was not the only one. There were several people who had reported people missing, and we were all invited to go there on that day to try and find the missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what scene did you see when you went to Djakovica; in particular, where in Djakovica did you go?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: In the Pastrik Hotel in Djakovica, on the ground floor of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what was there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Well, all the bodies that had been transported from the canal to Djakovica where the pathologists did their job were there, and I went there to identify the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you actually see any body of your father or any body that you identified as that of your father?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there any items of personal property there on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you make any identification?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you make any identification? Just answer me yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you identify your father's body?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see any personal property of your father?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember what that was?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Wrist-watch and clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Had your father had any operations prior to July 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of operations?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had leg surgery -- in fact, he had a hip operation. An artificial hip was implanted in his body.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know when that happened?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Five or six years before he went missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown Exhibits 65 ter 1368 and 1369, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the item in the middle that you can see depicted there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: It's a wrist-watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, it's a wrist-watch. Do you know by any chance whose wrist-watch it is?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: It was my father's.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And this -- 1369 I think is the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First we -- do you want to have the batch of photographs under one exhibit number, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: There's no point in having separate exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then already for you, Mr. Registrar, that would be the -- are these the second and the last?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, the second and the last.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the two, all together six photographs, would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the six photographs will be Prosecution Exhibit 343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And just on that last photograph, is that the same or is that -- in particular, the bottom one, is that your father's watch?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Last topic: Did you ever --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've done with those photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever obtain -- or, sorry, speak to anyone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I hope I'm not jumping in too soon in anticipating what this question is asking and seeking to elicit, but if it is seeking to elicit a certain hearsay account, I would wish to make an objection to it because of the nature and quality of the account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Stosic, the next question that will be put to you by Mr. Di Fazio you are invited not to answer immediately, but to wait to answer that question until I've invited you to do so. Mr. Di Fazio, if you put the question to the witness, then Mr. Emmerson will find out whether that is the question he expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, it's going to be that topic, I can indicate that, but I can proceed in the way that you, Your Honours, have indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Following this -- these trips to the canal that you've told us about and the -- your trip to the Hotel Pastrik, did you make any other inquiries concerning the disappearance of your father?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think that's a gentle question which is, as Mr. Di Fazio acknowledges, is heading in the direction in which I seek to raise my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's [indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to the form of that question but we're very shortly going to be in a position that Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But let's not at every question speculate on how close we are to the area of which you consider to be the area --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Did you make any other inquiries concerning the disappearance of your father other than the -- this visit to the canal that you've told us about and other than this visit to the Hotel Pastrik?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: Can I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: No, nothing after that. I just heard rumours, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Other than rumours, did you ever receive any information, apart from rumours, as to the circumstances of your father's disappearance?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then before we adjourn, two very classical questions. P341 is a photo of -- on which the witness identified his father, Velizar, any objection against admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P343 are six photographs, personal belongings of the victim. No objections, then P341 and 343 are admitted. 342 is the map marked by the witness, as far as I remember, Mr. -- or, no, we have not yet assigned a number to the marked map, did we? Oh, yes, I say "map," but of course it's an aerial view of the area which I, by mistake, called a map. P342, any objections against? No. Then P341, 342, and 343 are admitted into evidence. And Mr. Stosic, before you entered the courtroom the Defence counsel have asked whether they could put questions to you not immediately after you would have answered the questions by the Prosecution, but most likely either later today or tomorrow, perhaps most likely tomorrow. The Chamber will still have to decide on that request, so therefore at this moment I can't tell you yet whether immediately after the break you'll be cross-examined by Defence counsel or whether it will only be either later today or tomorrow. You'll be informed about what will happen immediately after the break. The Victims and Witnesses Section will tell you whether you're free to go then and to return tomorrow or whether we'd like you to stay and answer questions put to you by the Defence. Now, in case you would not be further examined today, I already thought possibly to instruct you that you should speak with no one about your testimony, that is, the testimony you have given today and testimony still to be given later today or tomorrow. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise that we have to keep you in uncertainty for the break. I hope that you'll get a cup of tea or a cup of coffee so that -- but you'll be informed immediately after the break or perhaps even during the break if the Chamber has decided whether or not to grant your request from the Defence. We stand adjourned until 4.25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All three Defence counsel, in order to avoid whatever misunderstanding, I've asked to make everything ready for the protective measures requested mainly because to remove it all, if you would not grant the motion, would take three or four minutes; to get everything in place takes approximately 25 minutes. So therefore, it's purely for practical reasons that you find already all preparations made, but of course first the Chamber would like to hear from the Defence their position in relation to the requested protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You anticipated my position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I did not at all as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What I was saying that in a positive light, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm not objectionable either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I think it would take us instead of 25 minutes only five minutes to finalise the protective measures. I take it that the curtains have to be drawn down and perhaps we ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber grants the motion by the Prosecution for protective measures, that is, in this case face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym. The witness would have the pseudonym 62. The Chamber will have a break for just three or four minutes in order to further prepare with curtains down and test the -- and test the voice distortion. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: There's -- there are a couple of matters that you raised earlier that I can very briefly deal with, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, the Chamber prefers at this moment to see whether we can get started. I already informed the parties that the next break will be at 5.30, that for urgent Tribunal matters, I'm not able to continue to sit after the break and that it's -- I understand that the two remaining Judges, but you'll hear from them, that they've decided in the interests of justice they would like to continue in my absence. I'll be back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just in terms of formalities I'm inferring from -- that the way Your Honour is proposing to deal with the protective measures implementation that you have acceded to the Defence's request in relation to postponement of cross-examination of the last witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, I thought that the parties would have been informed but -- because I instructed -- it was not easy to reach everyone, and I did not follow-up that in full detail but your suggestion has been followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I also infer, for the same reasons, that cross-examination of the next witness, were we to reach that position, would adjourned until tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we already instructed the Victims and Witnesses Section that the witness is excused for today and expected to come back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I didn't -- perhaps I wasn't clear. May I also infer given the issue of disclosure in respect of the forthcoming witness who has the benefit of protective measures that should we reach the position this afternoon where evidence in chief concludes, that cross-examination of that witness will take place tomorrow as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- it would be for both --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- testified already earlier today and now also for this witness now to be examined. Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're very quickly discussing the cross-examination of this next witness, I just wanted to ask for some guidance by the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber ordered in the future that at the beginning of direct examination of new witnesses, the Defence teams were to provide the Prosecution with a list of exhibits that we could refer to in cross of that witness. And I already -- I had an informal discussion with my colleagues at the break. If we can just get from the Trial Chamber a little further direction in that regard. Does the Trial Chamber refer to specific documents like, for instance, we will use this exhibit to cross this witness or is it just we will use exhibits that the Prosecution has given us already?
