If we can just get a little clarification from the Trial Chambers in that regard, I think it would help our -- the disclosure in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll tell you after the three- or four-minutes' break. --- Break taken at 4.37 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the curtains can be ... Witness, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 62, I'm calling you Witness 62 because the Chamber has just decided that it grants the protective measures you have requested. That means that no one outside this courtroom sees your face, that your voice will be distorted, as not to be recognised, and that we'll not call you by your own name, but we'll call you Witness 62. Witness 62, before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher, and I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I declare solemnly that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 62. Please be seated. Witness 62, would you please speak close to the microphone, and you'll now first be examined by Mr. Kearney, who's counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Kearney, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And excuse me, members of the Trial Chamber, I'm losing my voice today, so I'll do my best to retain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 62, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Good day to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- I'd like to call-up 65 ter Exhibit 1373, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's of course not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps we should go into private session for the first portion of this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We could do that, although the pseudonym sheet doesn't ask for it, but I take it that you have further questions then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, and my apologies for not waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 62, you just told us about the -- the four soldiers you saw at your home on the night in question. I just want to ask you if they were armed when they came into your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Three of them, yes. I couldn't see the fourth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: The one, the first who came up to the entrance, he had a pistol. The other one had an automatic rifle or perhaps a Kalashnikov.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did any of these soldiers say anything to you or say anything that you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I talked to them only when they took my parents, when they went into the car. They -- I just greeted them. I asked them, When will you -- when will you send him back? And they said they would send him back the next day, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did they tell you why it was they were taking your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: They said that they had been sent by the deputy commander, Rrustem Tetaj, because my parents -- this is a long story. Three days ago my parents had learned who had been -- who had been the one that had injured my brother, but they did not tell us, only my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Witness 62, thank you for that answer. We have part of your -- part of your statement has earlier been submitted to the Court, so I just want to talk about what happened on the night of July 12th for a moment, if I can, please. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: On the night when they took your parents, did they tell you why Rrustem Tetaj had asked them to take your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: No. They just said that my parents would know why Rrustem Tetaj called them, and I spoke to my father. And I think he said that this was because they had discussed earlier about who injured my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: On the night your parents were taken, did the soldiers tell you where they were taking your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: They said, To the headquarters in Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And you used that term earlier,"The headquarters in Gllogjan." What headquarters are you referring to, Witness 62?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Well, it was the command. There was KLA in the village but also in the district, but the main headquarters was in Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did the soldiers tell you anything about when or how long they wanted to keep your parents, or when they would be returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: When I asked them, When will you bring my parents back? They said, The next day, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you actually see your parents being taken away that night, Witness 62?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please describe for us how that was done, how they were taken away.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: We were speaking with each other, and then they got into the car - it was a 4-by-4 vehicle - the soldiers got into the car and my parents got into the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What type of 4-by-4 vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: It was a black car, we call it a jeep, a 4-by-4. There was a spare tire on the fifth door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Had you ever seen that vehicle before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After your parents were taken away that evening, did you ever see them alive again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After your parents were taken from your home that evening, did you have any further contact --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, with apologies, I think we may need to go into private session just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During this conversation, did he give you any more details about why your parents had been abducted from the home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: He didn't say anything. He only said that when he was returned he had met Rrustem Tetaj, and Rrustem Tetaj had told the soldiers to take him home and take my parents so that he could show them our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to talk about Rrustem Tetaj just for a moment now. After your parents were taken from the home, did you ever talk with him or meet with him after that -- after that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us where that was and when it was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I met him -- well, my parents were taken away on the 12th, so I met him about two days later. I had to go to the village of Lluka as a volunteer, to join. I was together with my brother and about seven or eight other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You said you were there as a volunteer to join, to join what organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: The Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And why were you in Lluka on that day in question two days after your parents were taken from the home? What was going on in Lluka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I went earlier to get information about this before my parents were taken away. I went there to meet Rrustem Tetaj and went together with other volunteers to get arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you met Rrustem Tetaj -- strike that for one moment. You said that you met him two days after your parents were taken. You've told us already, Witness 62, that that happened, your parents were taken on the 12th of July. Am I correct in assuming that you met Mr. Tetaj on the 14th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes, on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you met Mr. Tetaj on the 14th in Lluka, did you have a conversation about your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us about that conversation. What was said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I went there with another person. I can give you his name later to you, if needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'll put myself in the Chamber's hands. Do you want to have that name on the record now, or should we go on with the testimony? Perhaps for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps you give that name at a later stage when we are in private session anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: My only thought would be, just for clarity for the Trial Chambers, the story might make more sense to you if you heard the name now or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then let's do the following. We are closed to 5.30 where we have a break anyhow. So we turn into private session, we stay in private session for just a very short period of time, and after that we'll adjourn until ten minutes to 6.00. We turn into private session. Yes, and upon return after the break we'll be in open session, unless there's any reason to remain in private session, Mr. Kearney. So we now turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I see we are back in open session --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. And as mentioned before, we are sitting now with only two. Judge Orie is busy with urgent Tribunal business, and the two remaining Judges decided it to be in the interests of justice to continue on basis of Rule 15 bis. Please, Mr. Kearney, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 62, when we left off you had identified for us a person you were with in Lluka while you were talking to Rrustem Tetaj. Does that refresh your memory as to where we left off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you now if during this contact that you had with Mr. Tetaj you discussed with him your parents, what had happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us what was discussed between you and Mr. Tetaj regarding your parents.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: When I met Rrustem Tetaj -- when both of us met him, we asked him about my parents, and he addressed my friend and told him, Your father has come home. I've told my soldiers to return him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When Mr. Tetaj said that your -- your father had returned home, whose father was he referring to you, your father or the father of your friend who you identified previously while we were in private session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: No. I meant my friend's father. The father of the person who came, and then they took my parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you question Mr. Tetaj about your parents, not your friend's parents, your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes. I told him that the soldiers who came together with my friend's father, they all came to my house, and they took my parents away. And the soldiers said that, You sent them, that's what I told him. And he told me, I don't know about this. Who told you that I sent them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when he asked you that question, what did you say back to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I told him that the person who came to my house together with them -- and that person with the two soldiers had came to my house, and that person had come there to show them the house. He told me that, I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did he suggest to you any course of action, or did you discuss with him anything that could be done to try and find your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I told him, Because you took that person and you returned him to his home, and after he was returned he came to help them take my parents away. So you can -- you must help me to find my parents. And that person told me that they had been taken to the headquarters in Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you asked Mr. Tetaj to help you find your parents, what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: He said that, If you want to go to Gllogjan you can go, but you won't be able to come back alive. And I asked him whether -- well, are you the deputy commander of the zone? I want to go there and speak to the commander directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were those the exact words that he used, Witness 62, that: "You won't be able to come back alive if you go to Gllogjan," or did he use other words? Tell us what you remember, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Listen, he said, Well, you can go but for your own safety I cannot guarantee anything, because the commander of the area two days earlier had gone to help a group of the KLA who had been caught in an ambush, and Ramush Haradinaj had gone there to help them so Ramush Haradinaj is not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When Rrustem Tetaj told you that he could not guarantee anything if you went to Gllogjan, what was he referring to, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Well, what I understood him to say was that if you want to go you can go. I thought it was a threat, and that's why I told him, Are you a deputy commander? If the commander is engaged in a battle, you are the deputy. And he said, I'm not deputy commander or commander any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you said just a moment ago, Witness 62, that "you thought it was a threat," a threat from whom? Who did you understand it to be a threat from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Well, it was a dangerous time. That's what people said. If you did not have somebody strong to support you who had the authority in the headquarters to support you, then it would be difficult. That -- that's what people said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After Mr. Tetaj told you that, did you have any further conversation with him that day, on the 14th of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly. I think this was all we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After that conversation you had with Mr. Tetaj, did you inquire of any other members of the KLA about your parents after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes. When I returned from Lluka, we went to the villages. There was a headquarters of a couple of villages there, in the village of Vranoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you went to the headquarters in Vranoc, who did you talk to, if anyone, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I spoke to the commander of the area, and I explained him the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What was the name of the commander of the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: The commander of a unit was Mete Krasniqi, but the commander of the area was Dr. Din Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You said earlier, Witness 62, that you explained the case to him. Which person did you explain the case to, was it Mete Krasniqi or Din Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: They were, both of them, there. I talked to Mete Krasniqi first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us what you told Mete Krasniqi and what, if anything, he told you in response?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: In fact, I talked to Din, not Mete first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you the same question regarding Din Krasniqi. What did you tell him and what, if anything, did he tell you in response?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I explained to him that what had happened, I explained to him in detail what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did he respond to you in any way? What did he tell you in return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: When I explained to him about my parents and my case, he was surprised. He said he could not believe that these two people were abducted, and he said he had no information about that. He was very, very sorry. He said he would make inquiries about the case today, on the same day. He said he would go to the general headquarters on the same day. He would collect information, and then the next day he told me to come back to him so that I could learn about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you do that? Did you go back the next day and find out learn if he had learned anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes. I went there the next day. Din was not there when I went. I waited for some short period of time, and then he came later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you say Din was not there when you first arrived, where are you talking about, Witness 62, where were you waiting for him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: In the village of Vranoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And where within the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I was in the village of Vranoc at the place where the headquarters of this area was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This is the headquarters of the KLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, you said this was the -- the second meeting with Din Krasniqi was the following day. You told us earlier that your first meeting was the 14th of July, I believe. Am I correct in assuming that this next meeting with Din Krasniqi was on the 15th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us what happened when Din Krasniqi got back to the KLA headquarters in Vranoc on the date in question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: When he came we exchanged greetings, then we discussed. I asked him about any new information, and he said that he had gone to Gllogjan the previous night, to the headquarters, and that he had been told that my parents were in the headquarters in Gllogjan, they were interrogated there, and then they were released in Irzniq. So that was the information he had received the previous night. Then he also talked to me about another variant which he had learned about on the same day, the 15th. He said he received information that my parents had been taken to the headquarters and that somebody else had taken them away without the headquarters knowing it, and he said there was no information about their whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything more about who had taken them away from the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: He said that somebody had taken them away, and he said that no one in the headquarters knew anything about it. He said that that was all he could get from the people he had talked in the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did he tell you who it was that he had talked to in the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: No, he did not mention any name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did he say if the people he talked to were KLA soldiers or civilians that he talked to in the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: He said that he had talked to the members of the staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I just clarify. Witness, you were talking of the headquarters in Gllogjan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: But then you mentioned -- let us speak of the first version you mentioned, that they were supposedly released in Irzniq, that was what is on the record now. That sounds a little difficult to understand. Interrogated in Gllogjan and released in Irzniq. Can we maybe clarify that, Mr. Kearney, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'd be happy to, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 62, the -- the two pieces of information that Din Krasniqi relayed to you that he had heard about your parents, namely, one, that they had been interrogated in Gllogjan and released in Irzniq; and two, that they had been taken by someone from the headquarters, did he tell you which one of those he believed to be true? Did he tell you anything more about those two pieces of information?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the clarification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the clarification sought was how somebody who had been detained in Gllogjan could be released in Irzniq. I thought that that was Your Honour's question from the clarification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Absolutely that was the just of my question, but I thought that maybe Mr. Kearney wanted to take this route to get to this classification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And that will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It's true, we have two pieces of information, but the first piece or the first version consists of two elements, interrogation in Gllogjan and release in Irzniq. And please, Mr. Kearney, get to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Witness 62, the last question I asked you, let's keep that on hold for a moment. When Din Krasniqi was telling you about the first piece of information he had heard on the 14th of July, in the evening, about your parents; namely, that they had been detained in Gllogjan and released in Irzniq, did he tell you how that supposedly happened, how they were detained in one place and released in another?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he did, because I asked him. The first piece of information which I received on the 14th, I told him how could they be released in another village, in Irzniq? And he told me that he had received this particular kind of information the previous day. They were interrogated, they were not detained, they were simply asked questions, that's what he told me, and then they were released in Irzniq. To -- they were let to go back home. He said that today, on the 15th, this is the information I have. They were there. They were questioned, and somebody then had taken them away. This is the words he used, somebody took them away, but nobody in the staff knew anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I guess it's still confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The first piece of information he heard about the detention in Gllogjan and their release in Irzniq, did he tell you anything else about why your parents were supposedly released in Irzniq, as opposed to being released, say, in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: This is what I think, they were taken from my village, from my house, and then they were taken to the staff. How is it possible then for them to be released in Irzniq? So this is a question I put to him, and then he said that he was told one day before, this was the first piece of information. He said that they were taken to Irzniq and they were released in Irzniq. I asked him, Who? But he provided me no name, and then he talked to me about the second version and I, in fact, believed the second version was true. They were in the headquarters. So I was more inclined to believe the second version than the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, does that clarify the point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, please. Witness, you may give us a further explanation what led you to believe the second version as more probable than the first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believed the second version rather than the first one because from the village of Irzniq to my village, even if you walk it would take about three hours. So if you would release them in Irzniq, then in three hours' time they would have been back home. He did not tell me who had taken them to Irzniq. They were not my parents, the people he was talking about, so I believed that the second version was true, because my parents were not at home at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- Just for purposes of the record I object to that -- the question and answer on the grounds of relevance, just for the purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. That is -- you mean objecting to the clarification -- to the attempt to clarify that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To the question of belief, to the question of belief, which is really where this whole line -- where this whole answer -- questioned his belief, and I'm objecting on the grounds of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Does the Court wish a response? I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please, please respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: My response would be it's clearly relevant. He's trying to determine what happened to his parents, and I think the relevance is rather obvious at this answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to get into a colloquy with my colleague, but once again I make the objection and leave it at that. I make it for purposes of the record and nothing more, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It still can be ruled on that or has to be ruled on that objection. We would overrule that objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did Din Krasniqi tell you who it was he had talked to on the morning of July 15th when he went to the headquarters in Gllogjan to inquire about your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Who did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: He did not mention any name, but he said they were people of the General Staff, people of the command of the General Staff. He had talked to people of his own group. So the commanders of the districts, and also with the general commander, this is what I understood it to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When he told you he talked to the general commander, did he tell you a name, or did he just use the word "general commander"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: No, he only said that he had talked in the commands, in the General Staff, without mentioning any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did he tell you what, if anything, the General Staff told him about what they would do in relation to your parents?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, now I'm going to make another submission. We're moving truly far afield in terms of multiple hearsay, unidentified, unattributed, multiple hearsay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please, your response.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I would ask that the Trial Chamber to allow the witness to answer and assess the levels of hearsay in relation to how much weight to give to the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yeah, please, if you do that by clarifying the level of hearsay once more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Krasniqi tell you -- first of all, did he tell you if the members of the general command staff said anything further about your parents on July the 15th when he went to Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes. He said that he had discussed and inquired about the whereabouts of my parents. So he asked about where my parents were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you receive back any information that you -- beyond what you've told us already?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did he receive any information identifying who it was that, in the second version of events, may have taken your parents away from the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: He did not say it about -- he did not say anything about suspicions; however, I told him what I thought. I tried to help him to discover the circumstances. I suspected that it was due to some feud we had -- we had with the family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, could that answer be given some further clarification, please, rather than steered away from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Sure, I would expect that would --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour this was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- be a new line of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- this was covered rather extensively in the 92 ter document we submitted to the Court, but further on in my examination I will be talking about it again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: For --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you would that be fine for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I think probably for purposes of continuity of testimony, this would be the perfect time to deal with the witness's answer so that we have a basis for an understanding of why he was trying to assist Mr. Krasniqi in determining what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And may I add to that, I don't believe that it is correct to say that the 92 ter statement deals with this aspect of the conversation in which the witness explained his reasons and suspicions to Mr. Krasniqi as relating to some feud we had with the family. And rather than Mr. Kearney pick this point up in some other context, it is, in our submission, right and fair that if he's eliciting this evidence clearly, he now elicit from this witness what it was he said to Din Krasniqi given that we've already had certain evidence about belief as to what it was this witness suspected or believed in relation to this feud and what it was he told Mr. Krasniqi. It's essentially fair examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: With all due respect to my colleagues, Your Honour, I'm operating under a very tight time-line, as the Court knows. There are things that I need to get out of my examination. It's my intent to come back to this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please make sure that you will come back to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After this conversation with Din Krasniqi, at a later time, Witness 62, did you ever hear any reports about the recovery of the bodies of either one of your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I could not understand your question. On the same day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: No. In the future, at some point, did you hear any information about the recovery of the bodies of your parents?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I indicate for Mr. Kearney's assistance, since he's concerned about pressure of time, that I certainly - and I think it's the same for Mr. Guy-Smith - would have no objection to him leading in respect of the body recovery, if that gives him sufficient time to explore the issue that he didn't explore a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd be happy to lead. Thank you, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 62, at some point, did you hear from someone that on -- that an identification card of your mother had been recovered by Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: I had heard, so at the beginning of September -- this is what you are asking for, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Somebody had seen on television, and he said that the television speaker had mentioned the name of my mother, she had the ID with her when her body was recovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Based on your own knowledge, Witness 62, when your mother was taken from your home on the 12th of July, 1998, did she, in fact, have her ID card on her person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you hear that this identification card was found on the body -- or found on a body found in the canal leading to Lake Radonjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: They told me, people told me, people who had seen it on television, who had seen the Serbian television, the Belgrade. I do not remember the channel. I did not watch it myself. However, I did not believe them. I had not watched them, so if you don't see something with your own eyes, then -- this remained only words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move on to the potential motivation for the abductions. You mentioned earlier that you told Din Krasniqi about a potential motivation for the abduction of your parents. Can you please tell us more about what it is you told him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62
utterances.text: Din Krasniqi knew my parents, knew them well; he was a doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The court is adjourning now to tomorrow, Courtroom I, same courtroom, afternoon, and we will continue with Witness 62 for -- ten minutes is your estimate, Mr. Kearney?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, however, that's dependent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- on how freely I can get through the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Of course. But it will be a short while and then we will have an interruption for you, and later the day continue with the questions put to you by the Defence. Yes. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kearney, you had a question dealing with our -- the interpretation of our order --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- concerning the documents, you should know, which will be likely used in cross-examination. Is that still an open question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. I just seek clarification from the Trial Chambers in that regard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Just -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I attempted to get that information from my colleagues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: No. I would like to clarify, if necessary, that our order was intended to mean that a specified list of all documents and other material likely to be used should be given. And as far as this material is not on the 65 ter list, the relevant documents are to be released. Okay. So we may adjourn now, and see you in -- tomorrow at 2.15, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 13th day of June, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
